summary: The Envoy listener now reports a forward that reached a registered, live role holder but got no acknowledgement within two seconds as receipt_timeout instead of delivery_failed; delivery_failed keeps every never-forwarded case and no_holder keeps no-claim. POST /v1/messages/publish accepts an optional dedupe_key used verbatim, mutually exclusive with idempotency_key (400 naming both, nothing published); /v1/messages/send is byte-for-byte unchanged. PR #1079 at fc7c2ab3ae2f4fe3fe04c16c5be826ca4612fe72.

nats.go v1.50.0 Conn.Flush() is FlushTimeout(10s) and returns the same nats.ErrTimeout sentinel as a receipt wait, so keying receipt_timeout on nats.ErrTimeout treated a forward still buffered on a reconnecting connection as acknowledged-late (the reviewer found it). The fix is at the source: RequestCoreTo has its own sentinel from the receipt wait alone; the flush is FlushTimeout(time.Until(deadline)) behind a guard so a request whose window elapsed before the flush returns a descriptive error (not ErrBadTimeout, not the sentinel) and the call never outlives the window by 10s.

A jj restore of an uncommitted file during a fault injection reverts the whole file to the parent, not just the fault: the first negative control of this round took delivery.go back to the committed state and its GREEN edit had to be re-applied; the second fault was run only after the bus change was committed so restore had the right base.

changes: (a) The Correct: require the selected receiver to reply snippet now has the errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) -> receipt_timeout branch, matching roleTopicDelivery; every other RequestCoreTo error stays delivery_failed.

(b) The Guidance paragraph no longer claims a receipt_timeout holder has the envelope: the forward was published to a registered, live-looking holder and no receipt arrived in two seconds -- usually a busy holder, but a process that died inside the registry stale window times out the same way and never had it; the daemon probes to tell slow from dead (LEGION-101 contract) and treats a live process as having the message.

The closing sentence under the snippet was tightened for the same reason: a stopped holder is delivery_failed only once its registration has gone stale; a fresh-but-deaf one (slow or dead inside the window) is receipt_timeout.
